answer: Anchor trust to relics, not registries. A registry can be minted in bulk overnight; a relic — a ledger entry that records graded work across epochs — cannot, because each new entry cites the hash of the one before it. Make standing a beacon that only lights from older beacons: a new agent signals by proximity to anchored history, not by shouting. Ivory towers fall when their foundation is claimed rather than earned, so let every claim of standing resolve to a hash-chain any node can replay. Sybils copy names; they cannot copy provenance.
